source_refs.note: Topic 7.2.1, printed 'Types of Security Threads' for 'Threats' (PDF 179, printed 176).

blocks.text: The book describes five main categories of threat when using online services: spam, spyware, cookies, phishing and pharming.

blocks.alt: Left: five boxes for the common clauses of terms of use, user obligations, limitation of liability, privacy and data use, intellectual property and termination of service, each with an example, plus users' rights. Right: a table matching spam, spyware, cookies, phishing and pharming to what each does and its defence: spam filter, antivirus, cookie management, checking the sender and checking https and the padlock.
blocks.caption: Terms of use, online threats and defences (original diagram after topics 7.1 and 7.2).
blocks.long_description: Terms of use set out what users must do, limit the provider's liability, explain how data are used, protect the provider's intellectual property and say when an account can be closed; users keep rights to privacy, information and withdrawing consent. Spam floods you with unwanted offers and is stopped by spam filters; spyware secretly watches you and is caught by antivirus software; cookies remember logins but can track you, so manage them; phishing sends fake messages that pretend to be your bank, so check the sender and do not click links; pharming sends you to a fake copy of a real site, so check the address, https and the padlock.

blocks.prompt: List the five threats described in this section.
blocks.explanation: Spam, spyware, cookies, phishing and pharming.

items: Five threats: spam, spyware, cookies, phishing, pharming.
